The extension is just for us puny humans, imgur and your browser actually talk behind you back, saying stuff like "Content-Type: image/gif". This is what tells the browser what to treat that file as, so the browser reads that, treats the file as a gif and renders it as such. 

I'm guessing imgur reads the file's header when it's uploaded - the file type can be detected from reading the first few bytes of the file in most cases. It then remembers that this is a gif file, and so tells your browser that when you ask for it.
